OHDSI QueryLibrary Sticky Redesigns

Source: vignettes/v07_querylibrary_sticky.Rmd
v07_querylibrary_sticky.Rmd

The QueryLibrary integration distinguishes an upstream clinical question from its published SQL. The SQL is training/reference material and is never executed by the sticky redesign path. Instead, a typed recipe or plan defines the population and variables, the server prepares a person-local omop.table sealed for DP, and a pinned mapping fixes one of the seven sticky primitives and its longitudinal reducer.

The roles are those of DataSHIELD: the analyst chooses the question (the population, the derived variables such as an age at a public reference year, and the public bins or levels); the data custodian owns every privacy setting (whether DP is available, epsilon, caps and the community tools’ protection mode). No client argument changes those.

Automatic questions in 2.10.4

Common reviewed questions need no explicit preparation. With the default dsomop.tools.mode = "auto", the catalog routes protected distributions, record summaries and effects through their registered component contracts. Record summaries such as condition.duration_stats use capped record-weighted components (up to ten records per person) and public scales; unregistered scales retain histograms while moments remain unavailable. Demographic partitions use a complete public domain. The protection label identifies fixed synopses, heuristic realised-contribution reuse, or a mixed frame. No known-disclosive exact fallback is used when the protected route is unavailable.

res <- ds.omop.analysis.run("dsomop:condition.duration_stats",
                            params = list(concept_id = 201820))
res$pooled             # views derived from compatible pooled signed components
res$meta$protection    # per-site route, allocations and unavailable fields

Questions with an automatic equivalent list it in omop_querylibrary_sticky_catalog()$automatic_equivalent and when printed.

Sticky redesigns

The core never uses differential privacy (dsOMOP 2.8.0 and later): tables loaded with ds.omop.plan.execute() or recipe_execute() carry no DP provenance, and the server refuses them as DP inputs. A sticky redesign is released on a table prepared for DP from a typed recipe or plan (ds.omop.dp.prepare(), dsOMOP 2.9.1 or later). The release prepares it for you when the redesign carries its recipe.

This is deliberately not a QueryLibrary SQL runner or an arbitrary join/query gateway. An upstream ID selects only a reviewed semantic mapping; it neither submits the upstream SQL nor constructs a data-dependent query. Preparation and release remain two explicit, typed steps.

The client cannot choose epsilon, seed, nonce, privacy epoch or rerolls. Servers 2.10.3 and 2.10.4 report privacy_contract = "protected_release_fixed_basis_or_realised_v1". Fixed-synopsis releases share a registered public basis; realised-contribution reuse is heuristic and has no mechanism epsilon. Signed components are pooled only when the contracts and logical source identities are compatible. Old per-release payloads cannot be pooled with this contract; retain per-site results during an incompatible upgrade and upgrade both packages together.

Noise is generated deterministically on demand, with no stored answers, lifetime budget, query quota or privacy accountant. Exact support gates, overlapping scopes and evolving data prevent a general full-transcript DP claim. See the security chapter and server disclosure documentation for the scope and utility of each protected route.

catalog <- omop_querylibrary_sticky_catalog()
table(catalog$statistic)
#> 
#>           binary_rate      bounded_distinct          bounded_mean 
#>                     7                     1                     7 
#>  bounded_record_count categorical_histogram                 count 
#>                     4                    31                     8 
#>     numeric_histogram 
#>                    71

Every category domain, numeric/date break, bound, concept set, time window, ordering rule and record cap must be public and fixed before data access. Observed categories and data-dependent top-N selection are not valid inputs.

For example, PE12 can be redesigned as a coarse age-at-a-fixed-public-year distribution. This avoids placing exact birth components in the prepared table and uses public decade breaks:

age_at_2025 <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "PE12",
  variable = "age_at_2025",
  breaks = seq(0, 120, by = 10)
)
age_at_2025
#> OHDSI QueryLibrary sticky redesign: PE12 
#>   Primitive: numeric_histogram 
#>   Reducer: mean 
#>   Input: a table prepared with ds.omop.dp.prepare() 
#>   Automatic equivalent: ds.omop.analysis.run("dsomop:person.year_of_birth_distribution") (no preparation)
#>   Upstream SQL authorized: no

Give the redesign its recipe and release it in one call; the input is prepared on every server, released, and removed:

recipe <- omop_recipe(
  variables = omop_variable_age(name = "age_at_2025", year = 2025),
  outputs = omop_output(name = "ages", type = "wide")
)
age_at_2025 <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "PE12", variable = "age_at_2025", breaks = seq(0, 120, by = 10),
  preparation = recipe
)
result <- ds.omop.querylibrary.sticky.release(age_at_2025, datasources = conns)

The same step can be explicit, for example to release several statistics on one prepared table:

ds.omop.dp.prepare(recipe, out = c(ages = "DP_ages"))
result <- ds.omop.querylibrary.sticky.release("DP_ages", age_at_2025,
                                              datasources = conns)

The whole release population must be defined in the recipe or plan: filtering, merging or otherwise manipulating a prepared table drops its DP provenance. Preparation requires person-local lineage. Matching descendants and unsealed external frames are refused; an assigned age or date alone does not certify DP provenance. Use the explicit preparation route for the intended population.

Longitudinal numeric and categorical record histograms use a deterministic declared order and a finite per-person record cap:

monthly_conditions <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "CO19",
  variable = "month_number",
  breaks = seq(0.5, 12.5, by = 1),
  max_contributions = 12,
  order_by = "month_number"
)

Scalar record totals and site-local database-wide distinct drug cardinality are also available only as explicitly capped estimands. The latter uses a complete public vocabulary-derived concept domain and canonical server-owned ordering:

condition_records <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "CO10", max_contributions = 25
)

distinct_rxnorm <- omop_querylibrary_sticky(
  "DEX06",
  variable = "drug_concept_id",
  levels = public_standard_rxnorm_ids,
  max_contributions = 50
)

DEX06 is a site-local bounded distinct cardinality. It is not pooled across sites: there is no privacy-safe cross-site linkage to compute the concept union from those counts. Use pool = FALSE to retain site-specific cardinalities.

Exact ZIP, source/free-text labels and patient/event rows remain unavailable. They do not silently fall back to a different query:

omop_querylibrary_sticky("PE08")
#> Error:
#> ! QueryLibrary PE08 is blocked: exact ZIP geography.

Use omop_querylibrary_sticky_catalog(include_unavailable = TRUE) to inspect the complete 201-ID partition: 129 executable bounded redesigns, 54 vocabulary/reference metadata questions, and 18 blocked result shapes.
